bundles.evidenceText: abstract objects don't stand in causal relationships
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that eliminating causally inert abstract objects identifies the assumed transcendent cause as an unembodied mind or personal creator. No stated bridge concerns that personal-mind inference. This proposition can remain true whether the pro subsidiary-1 inference from a finite beginning and causal need to an uncaused, timeless, spaceless, immaterial cause is credible or not. The nearest competitor, support for pro subsidiary 1, is therefore excluded under the no-contact default.

bundles.evidenceText: the fine-tuning of the universe implies the existence of a designer of the cosmos
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that fine-tuning exhibits extreme improbability and an independent pattern, excludes necessity and chance, and indicates design. Its polarity is support for pro subsidiary 2, whose proposition is that intelligent design explains life-permitting fine-tuning better than necessity or chance; the assertion directly increases that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, support for the pro central bridge, is excluded because this move contacts only the fine-tuning line, not cumulative convergence.

bundles.evidenceText: without God to ground objective moral values good and evil as such would not exist
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that objective evil exists and requires God as its ground. None of the stated subsidiary bridges concerns objective morality, and this single moral inference does not express the cumulative or complete motion-level proposition. It can remain true whether any available cosmology, fine-tuning, or resurrection bridge is credible. The nearest competitor, support for the pro central bridge, is excluded because a supporting moral example does not inherit cumulative-bridge contact; the no-contact default applies.

bundles.evidenceText: there just is no plausible naturalistic explanation of these facts
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the appearances, the disciples' resurrection belief, and the other cited historical facts lack a naturalistic explanation and are explained by Jesus rising from the dead. Its polarity is support for pro subsidiary 3, the bridge identifying God raising Jesus as the best explanation of those facts; the proposition directly increases that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, support for the pro motion bridge, is excluded because this is one historical line rather than the complete motion conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: you can know that God exists wholly apart from arguments simply by immediately experiencing him
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that immediate personal experience can disclose God independently of argument. No stated subsidiary bridge represents the religious-experience line, and the assertion does not itself state cumulative convergence or the complete motion conclusion. It can remain true whether the listed cosmology, fine-tuning, and resurrection bridges are credible. The nearest competitor, support for the pro central bridge, is excluded because an individual experiential line does not inherit central status; the no-contact default applies.

bundles.evidenceText: these methods of acquiring and maintaining beliefs cannot be relied upon to deliver truth
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that similar religion-forming methods produce incompatible beliefs and therefore are unreliable. That proposition specifically undercuts religious experience and religious belief formation, for which no stated bridge is available. It can remain true without deciding whether the five listed lines collectively fail through the underdetermination and contrary evidence stated by the con central bridge. The nearest competitor, support for that con central bridge, is excluded because this subsidiary example does not contact the central cumulative inference; no contact is selected.

bundles.evidenceText: the rational attitude in the absence of a very strong case for the existence of a Christian God is to believe that there is no such thing
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the highly specific Christian-God hypothesis competes with many alternatives and consequently bears a very strong burden. Its polarity is support for the con central bridge, whose proposition invokes a strong burden for the specific Christian God because the relevant inferences are underdetermined; this general specificity argument makes that bridge more credible. The nearest competitor, support for the con motion bridge, is excluded because the move does not yet assess all cited evidence or state the complete motion-level result.

bundles.evidenceText: I've never experienced things coming into existence from nothing
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that ordinary causal experience concerns rearrangements of existing material and cannot establish causation for creation ex nihilo or for the universe as a whole. Its polarity is attack on pro subsidiary 1 because it directly undercuts the causal premise needed for that Kalam bridge, so the proposition cannot remain inferentially neutral to it. The nearest competitor, support for con subsidiary 1, is excluded by the rule that a direct criticism belongs to the bridge attacked.

bundles.evidenceText: it's impossible to have any confidence in tracing our physical theories back to or beyond the Big Bang
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the cited theorem establishes only a beginning of expansion, while contraction models and the breakdown of current physics prevent a firm inference to an absolute cosmic beginning. Its polarity is attack on pro subsidiary 1 because it directly undercuts that bridge's finite-beginning premise. The nearest competitor, support for con subsidiary 1, is excluded because that bridge concerns extrapolating ordinary causation to ex nihilo creation, not whether cosmology establishes a beginning.

bundles.evidenceText: the idea that a mind might exist in the absence of the entire physical universe is complete speculation
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that identifying a nonphysical cause as an unembodied mind is speculative and that such a cause could instead be beyond human categories. The stated pro subsidiary-1 bridge concludes only an uncaused, timeless, spaceless, immaterial transcendent cause; it does not include the further mind or personality inference. The criticism can therefore remain true while that listed bridge remains credible. The nearest competitor, attack on pro subsidiary 1, is excluded by exact proposition compatibility, so no contact is selected.

bundles.evidenceText: there is no one method which is common to all religions which leads to these conflicting beliefs
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that religions do not share one belief-forming method and that the speaker instead uses logic, evidence, and personal experience. This responds to an objection about religious-belief methods, but no stated bridge represents the personal-experience line. The proposition can remain true whether the con central claim about the five evidential inferences is credible. The nearest competitor, attack on the con central bridge, is excluded because this local methodological reply does not contact that bridge's stated cumulative failure; the no-contact default applies.

bundles.evidenceText: we've got good cosmological evidence that the universe began to exist
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem survives changes in the theory of gravity, supports an absolute cosmic beginning, and combines with the causal premise. Its polarity is support for pro subsidiary 1, whose proposition begins with the universe's finite beginning and need for a cause; the expressed claims directly increase that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, attack on con subsidiary 1, is excluded because the move does not address that bridge's ordinary-experience objection to ex nihilo causation.

bundles.evidenceText: we don't experience things coming into being without material causes
bundles.rationale: The move accepts the description of ordinary experience but argues that creation without either a material cause or an efficient cause is still more impossible, directly rejecting the skeptical use of that experience. Its polarity is attack on con subsidiary 1, whose proposition says ordinary causal experience does not establish causation for ex nihilo creation or the universe. This assertion directly reduces that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, support for pro subsidiary 1, is excluded because the expressed force is a direct rebuttal of the con bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: this constitutes a phenomenon which very naturally invites explanation in terms of a cosmic scale designer
bundles.rationale: The move asserts conditionally that precisely constrained, physically inexplicable constants would naturally call for explanation by a cosmic designer. Its polarity is support for pro subsidiary 2, the bridge claiming intelligent design better explains life-permitting fine-tuning than necessity or chance; the stated conditional supplies a direct design reason and is not compatible with complete inferential neutrality toward that bridge. The nearest competitor, support for con subsidiary 2, is excluded because this atomic move expresses the positive design implication rather than the later cautions.

bundles.evidenceText: there might be multiple universes such as a world ensemble an evolving sequence or a complex of bubble universes
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that cosmic probabilities are uncertain, deeper physics may explain the coincidences, and a multiverse could make life-permitting observation unsurprising. Its polarity is attack on pro subsidiary 2 because those claims directly supply necessity-or-chance alternatives and undercut the inference that design is the better explanation. The nearest competitor, support for con subsidiary 2, is excluded by the rule assigning a direct criticism to the bridge attacked, even though the proposed alternatives resemble the con route's positive formulation.

bundles.evidenceText: the fine-tuning argument does nothing to support the claim that God is good rather than evil or indeed morally neutral
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that fine-tuning cannot distinguish a morally perfect God from an equally powerful evil or neutral designer. Its polarity is support for con subsidiary 2, specifically its proposition that fine-tuning does not identify an omniperfect Christian God; the asserted symmetry directly increases that limitation's credibility. The nearest competitor, attack on pro subsidiary 2, is excluded because that pro bridge claims only intelligent design over necessity or chance and does not itself claim the designer is morally perfect.

bundles.evidenceText: there's absolutely nothing mysterious or contradictory about any of this
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that infinity-minus-infinity is undefined only because the corresponding equation has multiple solutions, not because actual infinity generates a contradiction. Its polarity is attack on pro subsidiary 1 because it directly undercuts the philosophical premise used to infer that the past must be finite. The nearest competitor, support for con subsidiary 1, is excluded because that con bridge concerns causal experience and creation ex nihilo, whereas this move addresses the separate finite-past premise.

bundles.evidenceText: that's not much of an argument I don't see any grounds for thinking that's highly probable
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that divine hiddenness supports nonexistence only if God's existence would probably produce more obvious evidence, and it denies that this expectation has been established. Its polarity is attack on con subsidiary 3, whose proposition treats opaque divine presence as less expected under a morally perfect Christian God than under atheism; the denial directly reduces that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, support for pro central, is excluded because rebutting one hiddenness inference does not state cumulative convergence.

bundles.evidenceText: identical quantities you subtract identical quantities and you come up with non identical results
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that applying transfinite subtraction to a real collection yields nonidentical remainders from identical starting quantities and removals, which it treats as absurd in reality. Its polarity is support for pro subsidiary 1 because this defends the finite-past premise used by that bridge; the proposition directly increases the credibility of rejecting an actually infinite past. The nearest competitor, attack on a con subsidiary bridge, is excluded because no stated con subsidiary concerns the arithmetic of an infinite past.

bundles.evidenceText: the issue of fine tuning is not likely to be resolved by a future physics
bundles.rationale: The move denies that fine-tuning probabilities are ungrounded and denies that deeper future physics is likely to remove the multiple, diverse fine-tuning cases. Its polarity is attack on con subsidiary 2, whose proposition invokes epistemic probability uncertainty and deeper physical explanations; these denials directly reduce that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, support for pro subsidiary 2, is excluded because the move is framed as a direct rebuttal of the con bridge's stated objections, despite also preserving a positive fine-tuning case.

bundles.evidenceText: there's no reason why an atheist has to presuppose that humans have no intrinsic value
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that atheists can perceive and accept objective moral values and human intrinsic value without God's presence affecting that perception. None of the stated bridges represents the moral-grounding argument. This proposition can remain true whether the available cosmology, fine-tuning, resurrection, or cumulative bridges are credible. The nearest competitor, attack on the pro central bridge, is excluded because criticism of one unlisted moral line does not inherit cumulative status; the no-contact default applies.

bundles.evidenceText: these are not independent reports but even so they contain many discrepancies
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the Gospel accounts are late, non-eyewitness, dependent, and discrepant, thereby undercutting the historical basis offered for the resurrection inference. Its polarity is attack on pro subsidiary 3 because it directly challenges necessary evidential premises of the claim that the empty tomb, appearances, and disciples' belief are best explained by God raising Jesus. The nearest competitor, support for the con central bridge, is excluded because this direct criticism belongs to the specific pro bridge attacked.

bundles.evidenceText: where would these come from if there is no moral lawgiver
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that atheism provides no nonarbitrary ground for objective moral value, obligation, or prohibition and that a moral lawgiver supplies such grounding. No stated subsidiary bridge contains the moral argument, and the move does not express cumulative convergence or the complete motion conclusion. Its proposition can remain true whether the listed cosmology, fine-tuning, and resurrection bridges are credible. The nearest competitor, support for the pro central bridge, is excluded because an individual unlisted moral line does not inherit central contact; no contact is selected.

bundles.evidenceText: the three facts that I mentioned are agreed upon by the majority of historians today
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the empty tomb, appearances, and origin of the disciples' resurrection belief are accepted even by the cited skeptical historians, countering the claim that Gospel discrepancies remove those facts. Its polarity is support for pro subsidiary 3 because establishing those historical premises directly increases the credibility of the bridge that God raising Jesus best explains them. The nearest competitor, support for the pro central bridge, is excluded because this move contacts only the resurrection line, not cumulative convergence.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't think you could infer obviously infinite power from fine-tuning
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that fine-tuning and the other presented arguments warrant at most a being of enormous power, not infinite power, which would require another kind of argument. Its polarity is support for con subsidiary 2, specifically the proposition that fine-tuning does not identify an omniperfect Christian God; the expressed limitation directly increases that bridge's credibility. The nearest competitor, support for pro subsidiary 2, is excluded because the move does not compare design with necessity or chance, even though it mentions an inference to a powerful being.
